codes.signedOut: You're signed out. Sign in again to continue.
codes.sessionExpired: Your session expired: you're signed out. Sign in again to continue.
codes.loginTimeout: Sign-in wasn't finished within {minutes} minutes, so it was cancelled. Try again.
codes.alreadyInProgress: Another operation on this lab is already in progress; wait for it to finish.
codes.noPasswordStored: No password is stored for this host. Edit it and enter one.
codes.portInUse: Host port {port} is already in use on this machine (another lab or app holds it). Stop whatever is using it, then start the lab again.
codes.dockerNotRunning: Docker isn't running. Start your container engine (Docker Desktop, or the docker service on Linux), then start the lab again.
codes.dockerDenied: Docker is running, but your account can't use it yet. Add yourself to the docker group in a terminal (sudo usermod -aG docker {user}), then log out and back in.
codes.dockerDeniedWindows: Docker is running, but your account can't use it yet. Add yourself to the docker-users group (in a terminal run as administrator: net localgroup docker-users "{user}" /add), then sign out and back in.
codes.toolMissing: `{tool}` is not installed or not on PATH
codes.downloadStalled: Downloading the lab's images stopped making progress (nothing new for {minutes} minutes), so it was stopped. Check your internet connection, then try again: what was already downloaded is kept.
codes.downloadFailed: Couldn't download the lab's images: {reason}. Check your internet connection, then try again.
codes.boxDownloadStalled: Downloading the lab's VM box stopped making progress (nothing new for {minutes} minutes), so it was stopped. Check your internet connection, then try again.
codes.boxDownloadFailed: Couldn't download the lab's VM box: {reason}. Check your internet connection, then try again.
codes.serverAuthFailed: Cyber CTF can't sign in to {server}: its token was revoked or its password changed. Update it in Servers.
codes.toolTooOld: This lab needs {tool} {required} or later, and this computer has {found}. Update it, then start the lab again.
codes.elevationFailed: Hyper-V needs administrator rights, and they couldn't be had ({reason}). Start the lab again and accept the prompt.
codes.labNotReady: The lab started, but didn't become ready: {detail}
codes.machinesGone: Some of this lab's machines are gone ({machines}): they were removed outside Cyber CTF, so it can't resume as it was. Start it again for a fresh copy.
codes.nothingToResume: Nothing is left of this lab to resume (its stopped containers or VMs are gone). Start it again for a fresh copy.
codes.notParkable: This lab can't be paused or shut down. Stop it instead.
codes.stepStalled: The lab's `{step}` step showed no progress for {minutes} minutes, so it was stopped. Its last output was: “{lastLine}”. Start the lab again; if it keeps happening, check the network and the resources of Docker, the hypervisor or the server.
codes.stepSilent: The lab's `{step}` step printed nothing for {minutes} minutes, so it was stopped. Start the lab again; if it keeps happening, check the network and the resources of Docker, the hypervisor or the server.
codes.stepCeiling: The lab's `{step}` step was still working after {hours} hours, the longest any step may run, so it was stopped. Start the lab again; if it keeps happening, check the network and the resources of Docker, the hypervisor or the server.
codes.stepTimedOut: The lab's `{step}` step ran into its {minutes}-minute limit, so it was stopped. Start the lab again; if it keeps happening, check the network and the resources of Docker, the hypervisor or the server.
codes.signInDenied: Sign-in was declined at Cyber Auth, so you're still signed out. Sign in again and allow Cyber CTF to continue.
codes.signInCodeUnavailable: Signing in with a code isn't available yet. Copy the sign-in link into any browser instead, on this machine or another.
codes.unreachable: Cyber CTF can't be reached ({detail}). Check your connection and try again.
codes.offlineReady: Cyber CTF can't be reached ({detail}). This lab is installed here, so it can start offline, without saving progress.

placementLockedHost.one: {count} lab is still on this host: stop it before changing its {fields}.
placementLockedHost.other: {count} labs are still on this host: stop them before changing its {fields}.

placementLockedAccount.one: {count} lab is still on this account: stop it before changing its {fields}.
placementLockedAccount.other: {count} labs are still on this account: stop them before changing its {fields}.

hostHasLabs.one: {count} lab still running on this host. Stop it before removing the host.
hostHasLabs.other: {count} labs still running on this host. Stop them before removing the host.

codes.labRunningHere: This lab is still running on this machine (or its machines are still there). Stop it, then try again.
codes.labRunningOn: This lab is still running on {host}. Stop it there, then try again.
codes.reapNoHost: No account is recorded for it, so the launcher can't destroy it. Remove its resources in your cloud console.
codes.pickCloudAccount: This lab runs in your cloud account: pick one of your cloud accounts to start it on.
codes.noHypervisor: No hypervisor ready on this machine runs this lab. Install one from the Machine page, or run the lab on a server or in your cloud account.
codes.virtiofsdMissing: {hypervisor} can't share your shared folder with the attack box: virtiofsd isn't installed. Install {hypervisor} again from the Machine page (that adds it), or run sudo apt-get install virtiofsd (sudo dnf install virtiofsd on Fedora), then try again.
codes.turnedOffByPolicy: Your organization turned this off on this computer (policy setting {setting}). Ask your IT team if you need it.
codes.tlsUnconfirmed: The certificate of {server} hasn't been confirmed yet (SHA-256 {presented}), so nothing was sent to it. To confirm it, open it in Servers, choose Edit, and compare the fingerprint with the one the server itself shows before you confirm it.
codes.tlsChanged: The certificate of {server} changed (it was {pinned}, it is now {presented}), so nothing was sent to it: someone may be intercepting the connection. If you replaced the certificate yourself, open it in Servers, choose Edit, and compare the fingerprint with the one the server itself shows before you confirm it.
codes.sshHostKeyRefused: The SSH host key of {host} isn't the one confirmed for it (or none was confirmed yet), so the connection was refused. If the server was reinstalled, open it in Servers, choose Edit, and check its new key.
